nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:hard-dist}
	There exists a family of distributions $\{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r)\}_{r \geqslant 0}$ over tripartite graphs with $n_r$ vertices in each layer, such that for $n_r > r^{4 \cdot 34^r}$, any deterministic protocol $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ with,
	\[
		\ensuremath{\textnormal{\textsf{round}}}(\ensuremath{\pi}_r) = r \qquad \textnormal{ and } \qquad \ensuremath{\textnormal{\textsf{suc}}}(\ensuremath{\pi}_r, \ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r)) \geqslant 15/16,
	\]
	must have, \[
		\ensuremath{\textnormal{\textsf{bw}}}(\ensuremath{\pi}_r) \geqslant (n_r)^{(1/2) \cdot (1/ 34^r)} \cdot (480)^{-2}.
	\]

nodes.statement: By the easy direction of Yao's minimax principle (i.e, an averaging argument), it is sufficient to argue that for deterministic protocols using o(log log n) rounds, O(log n) length messages are not sufficient to solve triangle detection with probability of success at least 15/16 when input graphs are drawn from distribution ensuremathG_r(n_r). In Crefthm:hard-dist, when r = o(log log n_r), we know that the initial condition of n_r > r^4 cdot 34^r is satisfied. The bandwidth required, however, is, \[ (n_r)^(1/2) cdot (1/ 34^r) cdot (480)^-2 gg mboxpoly log(n_r), \] which is more than the O(log n) bandwidth allotted in the CONGEST model.

In \Cref{thm:hard-dist}, when $r = o(\log \log n_r)$, we know that the initial condition of $n_r > r^{4 \cdot 34^r}$ is satisfied. The bandwidth required, however, is,
\[
	 (n_r)^{(1/2) \cdot (1/ 34^r)} \cdot (480)^{-2} \gg \mbox{\rm poly} \log{(n_r)}, 
\]
which is more than the $O(\log n)$ bandwidth allotted in the CONGEST model.

nodes.statement: In the following, we additionally condition on any fixed choice of (ensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^*) and assume this choice is known to all players. This can only strengthen the lower bound. First consider any vertex w notin setensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^*. If w outputs Yes, namely, that there is a triangle in G, then, by~Crefobs:tri-exist-0-round, the answer is only correct with probability 1/8 as the choice of edges between ensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^* is independent. So, we assume all vertices other than (ensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^*) output No. Now, consider any vertex ensuremathx^* in setensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^*. When degree of ensuremathx^* is anything other than two, it can simply output No and will be correct in this case. There are now two cases: item All vertices in setensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^* still output No even when their degree is two: in that case, the protocol always outputs No (by our assumption earlier) and thus is wrong with probability 1/8 by~Crefobs:tri-exist-0-round. item At least one vertex ensuremathx^* in setensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^* outputs Yes when its degree is two: in that case, with probability half the edge between ensuremathy^* neq ensuremathz^* in setensurematha^*,ensuremathb^*,ensuremathc^* may not appear, thus making the protocol wrong with probability 1/2 in this case. The probability that ensuremathx^* has degree two here is 1/4 and conditioned on this, its output will be wrong with probability 1/8. Thus, in this case also the protocol is wrong with probability 1/8 again. Overall the success probability of the protocol is at most 7/8.
nodes.raw_latex:
In the following, we  additionally condition on any fixed choice of $(\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*})$ and assume this choice is known to all players. This can only strengthen the lower bound. 
	
	First consider any vertex $w \notin \set{\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*}}$. If $w$ outputs \emph{Yes}, namely, that there is a triangle in $G$, then, 
	by~\Cref{obs:tri-exist-0-round}, the answer is only correct with probability $1/8$ as the choice of edges between $\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*}$ is independent. So, we assume all vertices other than $(\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*})$ output \emph{No}. 
	
	Now, consider any vertex $\ensuremath{x^{*}} \in \set{\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*}}$. When degree of $\ensuremath{x^{*}}$ is anything other than two, it can simply output \emph{No} and will be correct in this case. There are now two cases: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \emph{All} vertices in $\set{\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*}}$ still output \emph{No} even when their degree is two: in that case, the protocol always outputs \emph{No} (by our assumption earlier) and thus is wrong with probability $1/8$ by~\Cref{obs:tri-exist-0-round}. 
		\item At least one vertex $\ensuremath{x^{*}} \in \set{\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*}}$ outputs \emph{Yes} when its degree is two: in that case, with probability half the edge between $\ensuremath{y^{*}} \neq \ensuremath{z^{*}} \in \set{\ensuremath{a^*},\ensuremath{b^*},\ensuremath{c^*}}$ may not appear, thus making
		the protocol wrong with probability $1/2$ in this case. The probability that $\ensuremath{x^{*}}$ has degree two here is $1/4$ and conditioned on this, its output will be wrong with probability $1/8$. Thus, in this case also the protocol 
		is wrong with probability $1/8$ again. 
	\end{itemize}
	Overall the success probability of the protocol is at most $7/8$.

\end{align*}
where we bound the probability of a super set of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$. In $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$, fewer than $d_r \cdot (r+1)$ vertices are sampled from any layer $Y$ for any inner vertex $x \notin Y$. We will show that even if $d_r \cdot (r+1)$ vertices are sampled for each inner vertex, in addition to the set $\ensuremath{Y^{*}}$ uniformly at random and independently of each other, no vertex is sampled more than once except with a very small probability. 

We choose $2n_{r-1} \cdot (r+1) \cdot d_r  + n_{r-1} < n_{r-1}^{16} := \theta$ vertices uniformly at random and independently from $n_r $ vertices in layer $Y$. The probability that none of them are sampled more than once is,
\begin{align*}
\binom{n_r}{\theta} \cdot \theta! \cdot \frac1{(n_r)^{\theta}} &= \prod_{i=0}^{\theta-1} (1-i/n_r) \geqslant \exp\paren{-2 \cdot \sum_{i=0}^{\theta} i/n_r} = \exp(-(\theta-1) \cdot \theta/n_r).
\end{align*}

We do this for all three layers $A, B$ and $C$. The probability that no element is sampled twice in any layer is at least, 
\begin{align*}
	\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}] \geqslant	\exp(-3 \cdot (\theta-1) \cdot \theta/n_r) \geqslant \exp(-3/n_{r-1}^2) \geqslant 1-1/n_{r-1},
\end{align*}
where we have used the value of $n_r = n_{r-1}^{34} = \theta^2 \cdot n_{r-1}^2$ from \Cref{eq:params-r-1} and that $n_{r-1} \geqslant 3$. 

Conditioned on event $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$, we argue that the distribution of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r)$ and $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}}}_r(n_r)$ are identical. We already know that the distributions of the input of each inner vertex is marginally the same by \Cref{clm:sample-input-separate}. When $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$ happens, all the outer vertices have channel-degree at most one, and the neighbors of each inner vertex are disjoint barring $\ensuremath{X^{*}}, \ensuremath{Y^{*}}, \ensuremath{Z^{*}}$. This satisfies all the properties of instances sampled from $\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r)$. 

Let $\ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$ be the indicator random variable for event $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$. 
\begin{align*}
	\tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r)}{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}}}_r(n_r)} &\leqslant \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{I \sim \ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}} \tvd{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r) \mid \ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}} = I)}{(\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}}}_r(n_r) \mid \ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}} = I)} \tag{by ``overconditioning'' as in \Cref{fact:tvd-over-conditioning}}\\
	&\leqslant \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}} = 1] \cdot \tvd{(\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r) \mid \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}})}{(\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}}}_r(n_r) \mid \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}})} + \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}} = 0] \\
	&=  0 + \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\ensuremath{\rv{I}_{\textnormal{uniq}}} = 0]  \tag{conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$, the distributions are the same} \\
	&\leqslant \frac1{n_{r-1}},
\end{align*}
where, in the last inequality we have used our upper bound on the probability of $ \neg \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{uniq}}}$.

\label{obs:input-indep}
		We have the following independence properties for the inputs of vertices in graph $G \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}}}_r(n_r)$:

	\end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: First, we argue that all the inner vertices have access to all the messages they send and receive in the first round. For any message sent by inner vertex x to another inner vertex y, we use pair randomness between x, y to sample it in step (2) from Crefbox:r-1-step2-inner-msgs. Thus, both x, y have access to the message. All messages sent by any inner vertex x to any other inner vertex is known to x. All messages received by x sent by some other inner vertex y is known to x as well. The remaining messages that x sends to outer vertices, and all the messages it receives from outer vertices are sampled with private randomness in step (3) from Crefbox:r-1-step3-input-rest, and are all known to the inner vertex x. When the input graph G lies in the support of ensuremathG_r(n_r), the channel-degree of all outer vertices is at most one from Crefobs:G_r-degree. Therefore, any inner vertex x with outer neighbor u can simulate the messages u sends to x, as it has access to the entire input of u. As for the inner vertices, they have access to all their inputs. We have argued they also have access to all the first round messages sent and received by them at the end of step (3) of ensuremathpi_r-1. They can continue to run protocol ensuremathpi_r from the second round by simulating the behavior of all outer vertices connected to them. This proceeds exactly as in ensuremathpi_r till the last round, and the inner vertices can find the output of ensuremathpi_r (again, since they can fully simulate outer vertices).

nodes.statement: We will prove that protocol ensuremathpi_r-1 from Crefbox:r-1-final-all-steps obeys the conditions in the statement of the lemma. For the number of rounds in ensuremathpi_r-1, this is exactly r-1 as ensuremathpi_r has r rounds, and the first round messages are sampled without any communication between the vertices. The total length of any message sent in the r-1 rounds of ensuremathpi_r-1 is at most s, as all the messages sent by ensuremathpi_r are at most s bits. We know by Crefobs:r-triangle-exist that for the graphs in the support of ensuremathG_r(n_r), if protocol ensuremathpi_r outputs the correct answer, ensuremathpi_r-1 is correct in detecting whether a triangle exists as well. The output of ensuremathpi_r and ensuremathpi_r-1 are the same when inputs are sampled from ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalreal, by Crefclm:run-round2. Therefore, it is sufficient to lower bound the probability that ensuremathpi_r outputs the correct answer when the inputs and first round messages are sampled from ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake as opposed to ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalreal. We use Creffact:tvd-small to lower bound the probability of success of ensuremathpi_r-1 where ensuremathE is the event that the answer on input G_r-1 is correct: ensuremathtextnormalPr_ensuremathG_r-1[ensuremathpi_r-1 textnormal is correct] &= ensuremathtextnormalPr_ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake[ensuremathpi_r textnormal is correct] tagby the discussion above \\ &geqslant ensuremathtextnormalPr_ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake[ensuremathpi_r textnormal is correct] - tvdensuremathensuremathD^textnormalrealensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake \\ &geqslant delta - parenfrac1n_r-1 + 15 sqrtfracsn_r-1, where in the second inequality is by the assumption on the correctness probability of ensuremathpi_r and~Creflem:round-elim-distance. Finally, the protocol ensuremathpi_r-1 is randomized, but it can be made deterministic by fixing the random string by the easy direction of Yao's minimax principle, without changing its probability of success, rounds, and bandwidth. The different sources of randomness do not cause an issue, as the randomness in all of these sources can be fixed to be a particular string.
nodes.raw_latex:
We will prove that protocol $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$ from \Cref{box:r-1-final-all-steps} obeys the conditions in the statement of the lemma. 
	
	For the number of rounds in $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$, this is exactly $r-1$ as $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ has $r$ rounds, and the first round messages are sampled without any communication between the vertices. 
	
	The total length of any message sent in the $r-1$ rounds of $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$ is at most $s$, as all the messages sent by $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ are at most $s$ bits. 
	
	We know by \Cref{obs:r-triangle-exist} that for the graphs in the support of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_r(n_r)$, if protocol $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ outputs the correct answer, $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$ is correct in detecting whether a triangle exists as well. The output of $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r}$ and $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$ are the same when inputs are sampled from $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}$, by \Cref{clm:run-round2}. Therefore, it is sufficient to lower bound the probability that $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ outputs the correct answer when the inputs and first round messages are sampled from $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$ as opposed to $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}$.
	
	We use \Cref{fact:tvd-small} to lower bound the probability of success of $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$ where $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}}$ is the event that the answer on input $G_{r-1}$ is correct: 
	\begin{align*}
		\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}_{\ensuremath{\mathcal{G}}_{r-1}}[\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1} \textnormal{ is correct}] &= \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}_{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}}[\ensuremath{\pi}_{r} \textnormal{ is correct}] \tag{by the discussion above} \\
		&\geqslant \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}_{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}}[\ensuremath{\pi}_{r} \textnormal{ is correct}] - \tvd{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} \\
		&\geqslant \delta - \paren{\frac1{n_{r-1}} + 15 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}}},
	\end{align*}
	where in the second inequality is by the assumption on the correctness probability of $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ and~\Cref{lem:round-elim-distance}. 
	
	Finally, the protocol $\ensuremath{\pi}_{r-1}$ is randomized, but it can be made deterministic by fixing the random string by the easy direction of Yao's minimax principle, without changing its probability of success, rounds, and bandwidth. 
	The different sources of randomness do not cause an issue, as the randomness in all of these sources can be fixed to be a particular string.

nodes.statement: By~Crefclm:Dreal-Drealtil-close, we have \[ tvdensuremathensuremathD^textnormalrealensuremathwidetildeensuremathensuremathD^textnormalreal leqslant frac1n_r-1. \] Thus, we can focus on bounding the distance between ensuremathwidetildeensuremathensuremathD^textnormalreal and ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake and use triangle inequality. tvdensuremathwidetildeensuremathensuremathD^textnormalrealensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake &leqslant tvdensuremathwidetildeensuremathensuremathD^textnormalrealensuremathH_1 + tvdensuremathH_1ensuremathH_2 + tvdensuremathH_2ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake tagby triangle inequality \\ &leqslant 6 cdot sqrtfracs cdot (n_r-1)^5 (n_r-1)^6 + tvdensuremathH_1ensuremathH_2 + tvdensuremathH_2ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake tagby Creflem:hybrid-1-inner-msgs and Crefeq:params-alphabetagamma \\ &leqslant 6 sqrtfracsn_r-1 + 3n_r-1 cdot sqrtfracs cdot gamma_r cdot (r+1) cdot n_r-1alpha_r + 1 + tvdensuremathH_2ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake tagby Creflem:cH1-cH2-public-msgs \\ &leqslant 6 sqrtfracsn_r-1 + 3 cdot sqrtfracs cdot(n_r-1)^6 cdot (r+1) cdot (n_r-1)^32 cdot (n_r-1)^11 + tvdensuremathH_2ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake tagby Crefeq:params-alphabetagamma \\ &leqslant 6 sqrtfracsn_r-1 + 3 cdot sqrtfrac s cdot(n_r-1)^6 cdot (n_r-1) cdot (n_r-1)^3 (n_r-1)^11 + tvdensuremathH_2ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake tagas r + 1 leqslant n_r-1 for large n_r \\ & leqslant 9 sqrtfracsn_r-1 + 6(n_r-1)^2 cdot sqrtfracs2(beta_r + 1) tagby Creflem:cH2-cDfake-inner-msgs \\ &leqslant 9 sqrtfracsn_r-1 + 6 cdot sqrtfracs cdot (n_r-1)^42((n_r-1)^5+ 1) tagby Crefeq:params-alphabetagamma \\ &leqslant 15 sqrtfracsn_r-1, concluding the proof.
nodes.raw_latex:
By~\Cref{clm:Dreal-Drealtil-close}, we have
	\[
		\tvd{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}} \leqslant \frac1{n_{r-1}}.
	\]
	Thus, we can focus on bounding the distance between  $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$ and use triangle inequality.  
	\begin{align*}
		\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} &\leqslant \tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1} + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2} + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} \tag{by triangle inequality} \\
		&\leqslant 6 \cdot \sqrt{\frac{s \cdot (n_{r-1})^5}{ (n_{r-1})^6}} +  \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2} + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} \tag{by \Cref{lem:hybrid-1-inner-msgs} and \Cref{eq:params-alphabetagamma}} \\
		&\leqslant 6 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}} + 3n_{r-1}  \cdot \sqrt{\frac{s \cdot \gamma_r  \cdot (r+1) \cdot n_{r-1}}{\alpha_r + 1}} + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} \tag{by \Cref{lem:cH1-cH2-public-msgs}} \\
		&\leqslant 6 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}} + 3  \cdot \sqrt{\frac{s \cdot(n_{r-1})^6  \cdot (r+1) \cdot (n_{r-1})^3}{2 \cdot (n_{r-1})^{11}}}  + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}}  \tag{by \Cref{eq:params-alphabetagamma}} \\
		&\leqslant  6 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}} + 3  \cdot \sqrt{\frac{ s \cdot(n_{r-1})^6 \cdot (n_{r-1}) \cdot (n_{r-1})^3}{ (n_{r-1})^{11}}}  + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} \tag{as $ r + 1 \leqslant n_{r-1}$ for large $n_r$} \\
		& \leqslant 9 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}} +   6(n_{r-1})^2 \cdot  \sqrt{\frac{s}{2(\beta_r + 1)}} \tag{by \Cref{lem:cH2-cDfake-inner-msgs}} \\
		&\leqslant  9 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}} + 6 \cdot  \sqrt{\frac{s \cdot (n_{r-1})^4}{2((n_{r-1})^5+ 1)}} \tag{by \Cref{eq:params-alphabetagamma}} \\
		&\leqslant 15 \sqrt{\frac{s}{n_{r-1}}},
	\end{align*}
	concluding the proof.

By our notation, we have $\rid{y_i} = \ensuremath{y^{*}}_i$. 
	First, we have, 
	\begin{align*}
			&\mi{\rMinner{x}(y_i)}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid  \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}} \\
			&\mi{\rMinner{x}(y_i)}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid  \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}, \eqcolor{\rtypeval{x, y_i}}} \tag{as $\rtypeval{x, y_i}$ is fixed by $\rNinner{x}{}$} \\
			&= 	\mi{\eqcolor{\rmsg{x}{Y}{}[\rid{y_i}]}}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}, \rtypeval{x, y_i}} \tag{as $\rid{y_i}$ is the vertex in $G$ to which $y_i$ is mapped} \\
			&= \eqcolor{\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{t \sim \rtypeval{x, y_i}}}\mi{\rmsg{x}{Y}{}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}, \eqcolor{\rtypeval{x, y_i}= t}} \tag{by the definition of conditional mutual information}.
	\end{align*}
	We use $\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}$ to be the joint random variable $\rNinner{x}{}, \rid{w}$ for each $w\neq y_i$ and $w \neq x$, $\ensuremath{\bm{\mathcal{J}}_{\textnormal{all}}}, \ensuremath{\bm{\mathcal{K}}_{\textnormal{all}}}$, all random variables in $\ensuremath{\bm{L}_{\textnormal{all}}}$ barring $\rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i}$, all random variables in $\rNpub{x}$ barring $\rNbhood{x}{Y}{}[\rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i}]$, all random variables in $\rMpub{x}$ barring $\rmsg{x}{Y}{}[y_j]$ for $y_j \in \rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i} \cap \{<\ensuremath{y^{*}}_i\}$. 
	These random variables are bundled together because they are not relevant to the rest of the proof. 


	We prove the statement for each type $t$ separately. Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}$ denote the event that $\rtypeval{x, y_i} = t$. 
	We omit the superscript $ \rightarrow Y$ and replace $x \rightarrow Y$ by $\ensuremath{\vec{x}}$ to avoid the clutter. 
	\begin{align*}
		&	\mi{\rmsg{x}{Y}{}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}, \rtypeval{x, y_i}= t} \\
		&=	\mi{\rmsg{x}{Y}{}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \eqcolor{\rid{y_i}, \rid{x}, \rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i}, \rNbhood{x}{Y}{}[\rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i}], \rmsg{x}{Y}{}[\rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i} \cap \{< \rid{y_i}\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}}} \\
		&=	\mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{y_i}, \rid{x}, \rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}, \rNbhoodup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}] ,\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cap\{ <\rid{y_i}\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}}  \tag{changing superscript $x \to Y$ to $\ensuremath{\vec{x}}$ for readability}\\
		&=	\mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{y_i}, \rid{x}, \rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}, \eqcolor{\rNbhoodup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\}]},\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cap \{<\rid{y_i}\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}}  \tag{as $\rNbhoodup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]$ is fixed to be $t$, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}$ and thus conditioning on $\rNbhoodup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]$ is w.l.o.g.}\\
		 &= 	\mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{y_i}, \rid{x}, \eqcolor{\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\}}, \rNbhoodup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\}], \\
		 	&\hspace{85mm}\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cap\{ < \rid{y_i}\}],\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}} \tag{as $\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}, \rid{y_i}$ are fixed by $\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\}, \rid{y_i}$ and vice-versa} \\
		 &= \eqcolor{\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\} = P}}	\mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{y_i}, \rid{x}, \eqcolor{\rNbhoodup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P], \rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P\cap \{<\rid{y_i}\}]}, \\
		 	&\hspace{85mm}\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \eqcolor{\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\} = P}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}}. \tag{by the definition of conditional mutual information}
		\end{align*}
		Again, we prove the statement for every set $P \subset [n_r]$ of size $\gamma_r + 1$. Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$ be the event that $\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\} = P$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_t}$ happen. 
		
		We argue that conditioned $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$, the value of $\rid{y_i}$ is uniform over the set $P$. This is because, by the definition of $\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}$, for all $y_j \in \rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}$, the value of $\Nbhood{x}{Y}{}[y_j]  = t$, similar to $\rNbhood{x}{Y}{}[\rid{y_i}]$. 
		The random variable $\rid{y_i}$ is uniform over $[n_r]$, and $\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i}$ is a uniformly random set of size $\gamma_r$ that does not contain $\rid{y_i}$. If $P$ is the set $\rLupdown{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\}$, the value of $\rid{y_i}$ can be any value in this set with equal probability. As such, continuing the above equations for any fixed $P$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$, we will get, 
		\begin{align*}
				&\mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[\rid{y_i}]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{y_i}, \rid{x}, \rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P\cap \{<\rid{y_i}\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \\
				&= \eqcolor{\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{y_j \in P}} \mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[y_j]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{x}, \rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P\cap \{<y_j\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}},  \eqcolor{\rid{y_i} = y_j}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \\
				&= \eqcolor{\frac1{\gamma_r+1} \cdot \sum_{y_j \in P}} \mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[y_j]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{x}, \rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P\cap \{<y_j\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}},  \rid{y_i} = y_j, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}}.  \tag{as $\rid{y_i}$ is uniform over $P$}
			\end{align*}
	Now, we argue that the event $\rid{y_i}  = y_j$ is independent of the joint distribution of all the other random variables in the mutual information term, conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$. 
	Let us list these random variables, and argue in steps (in each step, we condition on everything in the previous steps also). 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item $\rid{w}$ for $w \neq y_i$: these are disjoint from $P$ and independent of the identity of $y_i$ inside $P$. 
		\item $\rNbhood{x}{Y}{}[P]$: this is deterministically fixed to all be $t$ conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$.
		\item $\rNbhood{x}{Y}{}$: the input of $x$ to layer $Y$ is already fixed to be type $t$ for all elements of $P$. The rest of the input is independent of \emph{which} of these choices are the actual identity of $y_i$. 
		\item $\rNbhood{x}{Z}{}$: the input of $x$ to layer $Z$ is independent of which of the identities in $P$ belong to $y_i$. 
		\item $\rmsg{x}{Y}{}, \rmsg{x}{Z}{}$: we know the inputs of $x$ are independent of the event $\rid{y_i} = y_j$. As protocol $\ensuremath{\pi}_r$ is deterministic, the messages sent by $x$ are independent of this event also. 
		\item $\ensuremath{\bm{\mathcal{J}}_{\textnormal{all}}}, \ensuremath{\bm{\mathcal{K}}_{\textnormal{all}}}$: these are sets which are disjoint from $P$, and are also independent of $\rid{y_i} = y_j$.
		\item $\rNinner{x}{}$: this input to $x$ comes from $G_{r-1}$, which is independent of the identity of $y_i$. 
		\item $\rNpub{x}$ barring $\rNbhood{x}{Y}{}[P]$: this is comprised of inputs chosen for $x$ on sets disjoint from $P$ and are independent of which identity in $P$ is given to $y_i$. 
		\item $\ensuremath{\bm{L}_{\textnormal{all}}}$ barring $\rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i}$: these are all sets disjoint from $P$, independent of what happens inside $P$. 
		\item $\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}$: we have argued that all the random variables in $\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}} $ are independent of $P$.
	\end{itemize}
	As such, the joint distribution of these random variables is independent of the event $\rid{y_i} = y_j$ conditioned on $\ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$. 
	Hence, we can continue as,
		\begin{align*}
			& \frac1{\gamma_r+1} \cdot \sum_{y_j \in P}  \mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[y_j]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{x}, \rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P\cap \{<y_j\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}},  \rid{y_i} = y_j, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \\
			& = \frac1{\gamma_r+1} \cdot \sum_{y_j \in P}  \mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[y_j]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{x}, \ensuremath{\bm{\mathcal{M}}}[P\cap \{<y_j\}], \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \tag{as $\rid{y_i} = y_j$ is independent of all random variables together conditioned on $ \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$} \\
			&=  \frac1{\gamma_r+1} \cdot  \mi{\rmsgup{\ensuremath{\vec{x}}}[P]}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid \rid{x}, \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{rest}}}, \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \tag{by the chain rule of mutual information in \Cref{fact:it-facts}-(\ref{part:chain-rule})\xspace} \\
			&\leqslant \frac1{\gamma_r + 1} \cdot \en{\rMinner{x}(-y_i) \mid \ensuremath{\mathcal{E}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \tag {by \Cref{fact:it-facts}-(\ref{part:info-entropy})\xspace} \\
			&\leqslant \frac1{\gamma_r + 1} \cdot 2n_{r-1} \cdot s. \tag{as $\rMinner{x}(-y_i)$ has $2n_{r-1}-1$ messages of length at most $s$ sent by $x$}
	\end{align*}
	Putting things together, we have, 
	\begin{align*}
	&	\mi{\rMinner{x}(y_i)}{\rMinner{x}(-y_i)\mid  \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}} \\
	&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\substack{\rtypeval{x, y_i} \\ = t}} ~ \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\substack{\rLupdown{x \to Y}{t, i} \cup \{\rid{y_i}\} \\ = P}} \bracket{\frac1{\gamma_r + 1} \cdot 2n_{r-1} \cdot s} \tag{by all the bounds above} \\
	&\hspace{30pt}= \frac1{\gamma_r + 1} \cdot 2n_{r-1} \cdot s.
	\end{align*}
This completes the proof.

\label{obs:inter-hybrid-list}
About random variables associated with $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\roman*)$]
\item \label{item:hybrid1-1}	The random variable $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ is distributed the same way in $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$.
\item \label{item:hybrid1-2} In both $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, $\rv{w}^{w} \perp \rv{w}^{w'} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ for any distinct pair of inner vertices $w, w' \in A \cup B \cup C$. This is true regardless of whether $w, w'$ are in the same layer or in different layers. 
\item \label{item:hybrid1-3} 	Conditioned on any choice of random variable $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ and $\rv{w}^{x}$ for all inner vertices $x$, distribution of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}}$ is the same in $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$. 
\item \label{item:hybrid1-4} In distribution $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, for any inner vertex $x$, $\rv{w}^{x} \perp \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} \mid \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}$. 
\item \label{item:hybrid1-5} In distribution $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, for any inner vertex $x$, $\rv{w}^{x\to w} \perp \rv{w}^{x \to w'} \mid \rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}$, for any distinct pair of inner vertices $w, w' \in Y \cup Z$ of $G_{r-1}$. Again, $w$ and $w'$ may be in the same layer or different layers.
\end{enumerate}

Part \ref{item:hybrid1-1} is apparent from the definition of distributions $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, as all random variables in $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ are sampled the same way in $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$.

For part \ref{item:hybrid1-2}, we know that when $\rv{w}^{w}$ is sampled in $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$, it is sampled conditioned on random variables $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}},  \rNinner{w}{}$, $\rNpub{w}$, and $\rMpub{w}$ and $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}$. All these random variables are fixed by $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$. Thus, $\rv{w}^{w}$ and $\rv{w}^{w'}$ are independent for two distinct inner vertices $w, w'$ conditioned on $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ in distribution $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$. 

Similarly in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, random variable $\rv{w}^{w}$ is sampled only conditioned on $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}},  \rNinner{w}{}$, $\rNpub{w}$, and $\rMpub{w}$, all of which are fixed by $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$.

Part \ref{item:hybrid1-3} is clear, again from the definition of $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$ as $\rNrest{x}$ is sampled the same way in the two distributions for all inner vertices $x$ for any choice of the other random variables. 

Part \ref{item:hybrid1-4} is evident from how $\rv{w}^{x}$ are sampled. They are conditioned only on $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}},  \rNinner{x}{}$, $\rNpub{x}$, and $\rMpub{x}$ and are independent of the other random variables in $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$.

For part \ref{item:hybrid1-5}, in distribution $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, we know that when $\rv{w}^{x \to w} = \rMinner{x}(w)$ is sampled, it is conditioned only on $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}},  \rNinner{x}{}$, $\rNpub{x}$, and $\rMpub{x}$. It is independent of the messages sent by $x$ to other inner vertices, conditioned on these random variables.

nodes.raw_latex:
Let $u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_{2n_{r-1}}$ be all the inner vertices not in the same layer as $x$, following the ordering we defined.
We use $\rv{w}^j$ to denote the random variable $\rv{w}^{x\to u_j}$ for $j \in [2n_{r-1}]$. We use $\rv{w}^0$ to denote $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$. We use $\rv{w}^{<j}$ to denote the random variables $\rv{w}^0, \rv{w}^1, \ldots \rv{w}^{j-1}$.
We have, 
\begin{align*}
&\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}} \tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{x} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} )}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{x} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} )} \\
&\leqslant  \sum_{j \in [2n_{r-1}]} \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{<j}\sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}} \tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j} )} \tag{by the weak chain rule of total variation distance \Cref{fact:tvd-chain-rule}}\\
&\leqslant \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sum_{j \in [2n_{r-1}]}  \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{<j}\sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}} \sqrt{\kl{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j} )}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j} )}} \tag{by Pinsker's inequality \Cref{fact:pinskers}} \\
&\leqslant \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sum_{j \in [2n_{r-1}]}  \sqrt{ \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{<j}\sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}} \kl{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j} )}}. \tag{by Jensen's inequality and concavity of square root} 
\end{align*}

We bound the KL-divergence term separately for each $j \in [2n_{r-1}]$. 
Let us use $\rMinner{x}(< u_{j})$ to denote the random variables $\rMinner{x}(u_1), \rMinner{x}(u_2), \ldots, \rMinner{x}(u_{j-1})$.  We use $\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}}$ to denote the random variables $\ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}},$ $ \rNinner{x}{}, \rNpub{x}$, and $\rMpub{x}$ as they always appear in the conditioning.

We know by \Cref{obs:inter-hybrid-list}-\ref{item:hybrid1-4} that the distribution of $\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j}$ in $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}$ is,

\[
	\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j}) = \rMinner{x}(u_j) \mid \rMinner{x}(< u_j),  \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}}.
\]

We know by \Cref{obs:inter-hybrid-list}-\ref{item:hybrid1-5} and \ref{item:hybrid1-4} that the distribution of $\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j}$ in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$ is, 

\[
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j}) =  \rMinner{x}(u_j) \mid \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}}.
\]

Combining the above two equations gives us, 

\begin{align*}
&\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{<j}\sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}	\kl{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^j \mid \rv{w}^{<j} )} \\
&\hspace{30pt}= \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rMinner{x}(<u_j), \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \kl{\rMinner{x}(u_j) \mid\rMinner{x}(<u_j),\ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}} }{\rMinner{x}(u_j) \mid \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \\
&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant \mi{\rMinner{x\to u_j}}{\rMinner{x}(<u_j) \mid  \ensuremath{\rv{W}_{\textnormal{cond}}}} \tag{by \Cref{fact:kl-info}} \\

Let $u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_{3n_{r-1}}$ be the inner vertices with the lexicographic ordering. We use $\rv{w}^{u_{<\ell}}$ to denote the joint random variable $\rv{w}^{u_1}, \rv{w}^{u_2}, \ldots, \rv{w}^{u_{\ell-1}}$ for $\ell \in [3n_{r-1}]$. We use $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}}$ to denote all $\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}}$ for $\ell \in [3n_{r-1}]$. Using \Cref{fact:tvd-chain-rule}, we get, 
	\begin{align*}
		&\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant \tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})} + \sum_{\ell \in [3n_{r-1}]} \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{u_{< \ell}} \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}} \mid \rv{w}^{u_{<\ell}})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}} \mid \rv{w}^{u_{< \ell}})} \\
		& \hspace{60pt} + 	\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}} \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}	\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}},\rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid  \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}})} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}= \eqcolor{0} + \sum_{\ell \in [3n_{r-1}]} \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{u_{< \ell}} \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}} \mid \rv{w}^{u_{<\ell}})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}} \mid \rv{w}^{u_{< \ell}})}  \\
		& \hspace{60pt} + 	\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}} \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}	\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}},\rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid  \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{all}})}  \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-hybrid-list}-\ref{item:hybrid1-1}, we know $\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})$ are the same distribution}  \\
		&\hspace{30pt}= \sum_{\ell \in [3n_{r-1}]} \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{u_{< \ell}} \sim \ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}\tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}} \mid \rv{w}^{u_{<\ell}})}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{u_{\ell}} \mid \rv{w}^{u_{< \ell}})} + \eqcolor{0} \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-hybrid-list}-\ref{item:hybrid1-3}, distribution of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}}$ is the same} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}= \sum_{\ell \in [3n_{r-1}]} \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} \sim {\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}}} \tvd{\ensuremath{\widetilde{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{real}}}}}(\rv{w}^{x} \mid \eqcolor{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}} )}{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1(\rv{w}^{x} \mid \eqcolor{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}} )} \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-hybrid-list}-\ref{item:hybrid1-2}} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant (3n_{r-1})  \cdot 2 \cdot (n_{r-1})^{3/2} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{s}{\gamma_r + 1}} \tag{by \Cref{clm:inter-hybrid-1}} \\
		&\hspace{30pt} = 6 \cdot (n_{r-1})^{5/2} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{s}{\gamma_r + 1}}. \qedhere
	\end{align*}

About random variables $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^x$ for each inner vertex $x$ and $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}}$, in distributions $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$, we have, 
\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\roman*)$]

This is because all the random variables $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}$ and $\rNinner{x}{}$ for each inner vertex $x$ are fixed when conditioned on $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$. 
\item \label{item:wx-indep-H1} In $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$, random variable $\rv{w}^x$ is independent of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ when conditioned on $\rNinner{x}{} , \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}$ and $\ensuremath{\rv{aux}}$. 
\item \label{item:wx-indep-H2} In $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$, random variable $\rv{w}^x$ is independent of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ when conditioned on $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}$ and $\ensuremath{\rv{aux}}$.
\item \label{item:wend-indep-H1H2} Conditioned on any choice of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ and $\rv{w}^x$ for each inner vertex $x$, the distribution of random variable $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}}$ is the same in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_1$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$. 
\end{enumerate}

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{obs:inter-H2fake-list}
	About random variables $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^{x \to y}$ for each pair of inner vertices $x, y$ in different layers and $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}}$, in distributions $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$ and $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$, we have, 
	\begin{enumerate}[label=$(\roman*)$]
		\item \label{item:wstart-same-H2fake} In $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$ and $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$, the distribution of random variable $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ is the same. 
		\item \label{item:wxy-indep-H2fake} In $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$ and $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$, the random variables $\rv{w}^{i}$ and $\rv{w}^{j}$ are independent of each other conditioned on $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ for any $i \neq j$, $i,j \in [6(n_{r-1})^2]$. Random variable $\rv{w}^{x \to y}$ is sampled only conditioned on $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}$ and $\rNinner{x}{}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}$ for each inner vertex $x$, all of which are fixed when conditioned on variable $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$. 
		\item \label{item:wxy-indep-H2} In $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$, random variable $\rv{w}^{x \to y}$ is independent of the rest of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ when conditioned on $\rNinner{x}{} , \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}$, $\rNpub{x}$ and $\rMpub{x}$ inside $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$. 
		\item \label{item:wxy-indep-fake} In $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$, random variable $\rv{w}^{x \to y}$ is independent of the rest of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ when conditioned on $\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rtypeval{x, y}$ and $\rMpub{x}$ inside $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$.
		\item \label{item:wend-indep-H2fake} Conditioned on any choice of $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}$ and $\rv{w}^{x \to y}$ all pairs of inner vertices $x, y$ in different layers, the distribution of random variable $\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}}$ is the same in $\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2$ and $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}$. 
	\end{enumerate}

Hence the total variation distance term becomes, &ensuremathE_rvw^textnormalstart, rvw^1, ldots, rvw^ell-1 sim ensuremathH_2 tvdensuremathH_2(rvw^ell mid rvw^1, ldots, rvw^ell-1, rvw^textnormalstart)ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake(rvw^ell mid rvw^1, ldots, rvw^ell-1, rvw^textnormalstart) \\ &hspace30pt= ensuremathE_rvw^textnormalstartsim ensuremathH_2 tvdensuremathH_2(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart)ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart) tagby the equalities above \\ &hspace30ptleqslant frac1sqrt2 cdot ensuremathE_rvw^textnormalstart sim ensuremathH_2 sqrtklensuremathH_2(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart)ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart) tagby Pinsker's inequality in Creffact:pinskers\\ &hspace30ptleqslant frac1sqrt2 cdot sqrt ensuremathE_rvw^textnormalstart sim ensuremathH_2 klensuremathH_2(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart)ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart) tagby Jensen's inequality and concavity of square root \\ &hspace30pt= frac1sqrt2 cdot sqrt ensuremathE_rvw^textnormalstart sim ensuremathH_2 kl(rMinnerx(y) mid eqcolorrNinnerx, rNpubx, rMpubx, ensuremathrvids, ensuremathrvaux)ensuremathensuremathD^textnormalfake(rvw^ell mid rvw^textnormalstart) tagby Crefobs:inter-H2fake-list- \\ hspace30pt&= frac1sqrt2 cdot sqrt ensuremathE_substackensuremathrvids, ensuremathrvaux, rNinnerx, \\ rMpubx, rNpubx klrMinnerx(y) mid substackrNinnerx, ensuremathrvids, ensuremathrvaux, \\ rNpubx, rMpubxrMinnerx(y) mid eqcolorsubstackensuremathrvids, ensuremathrvaux, rMpubx, \\ rNpubx, rtypevalx,y tagby Crefobs:inter-H2fake-list-\\ &hspace30pt = frac1sqrt2 cdot sqrtmirMinnerx(y)rNinnerx mid ensuremathrvids, ensuremathrvaux, rNpubx, rMpubx, rtypevalx, y tagby relation between KL-Divergence and mutual information in Creffact:kl-info \\ &hspace30ptleqslant frac1sqrt2 cdot sqrtfracsbeta_r + 1. qedhere tagby Crefclm:mi-low-inner-msgs qedhere

Let $\rv{w}^{\ell} = \rv{w}^{x \to y}$.
	Firstly, by \Cref{obs:inter-H2fake-list}-\ref{item:wxy-indep-H2fake}, we have, 
	\begin{align*}
	\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}) &= \ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid  \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}), \quad \text{and} \\
		\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}) &= \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid  \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}).
	\end{align*}
	Hence the total variation distance term becomes, 
	\begin{align*}
		&\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1} \sim \ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}	\tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1}, \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}=	\ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}\sim \ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}	\tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid  \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid  \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})} \tag{by the equalities above} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} \sim \ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2} \sqrt{\kl{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}} \tag{by Pinsker's inequality in \Cref{fact:pinskers}}\\
		&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sqrt{ \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} \sim \ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2} \kl{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}} \tag{by Jensen's inequality and concavity of square root} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}= \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sqrt{ \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}} \sim \ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2} \kl{(\rMinner{x}(y) \mid \eqcolor{\rNinner{x}{}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}} \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-H2fake-list}-\ref{item:wxy-indep-H2}} \\
		\hspace{30pt}&= \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sqrt{ \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{\substack{\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNinner{x}{}, \\ \rMpub{x}, \rNpub{x} }} \kl{\rMinner{x}(y) \mid \substack{\rNinner{x}{}, \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \\ \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}}}{\rMinner{x}(y) \mid \eqcolor{\substack{\ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rMpub{x}, \\ \rNpub{x}, \rtypeval{x,y}}}}} \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-H2fake-list}-\ref{item:wxy-indep-fake}}\\
		&\hspace{30pt} =  \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sqrt{\mi{\rMinner{x}(y)}{\rNinner{x}{} \mid \ensuremath{\rv{ids}}, \ensuremath{\rv{aux}}, \rNpub{x}, \rMpub{x}, \rtypeval{x, y}}}   \tag{by relation between KL-Divergence and mutual information in \Cref{fact:kl-info}} \\
		&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant \frac1{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{s}{\beta_r + 1}}. \qedhere \tag{by \Cref{clm:mi-low-inner-msgs}} \qedhere
		\end{align*}

\begin{align*}
	& \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}} \\
	&\hspace{30pt}= \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}})} \\
	&\hspace{60pt} + \sum_{\ell \in [6(n_{r-1})^2]} \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1})} \\
	&\hspace{90pt} + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{6(n_{r-1})^2})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{6(n_{r-1})^2})} \tag{by \Cref{fact:tvd-chain-rule}}\\
	&\hspace{30pt}=  \eqcolor{0} + \sum_{\ell \in [6(n_{r-1})^2]} \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1})} \\
	&\hspace{60pt} + \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{6(n_{r-1})^2})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\textnormal{end}} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{6(n_{r-1})^2})} \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-H2fake-list}-\ref{item:wstart-same-H2fake}} \\
	&\hspace{30pt}=  \sum_{\ell \in [6(n_{r-1})^2]} \tvd{\ensuremath{\mathcal{H}}_2(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1})}{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathcal{D}}^{\textnormal{fake}}}(\rv{w}^{\ell} \mid \rv{w}^{\textnormal{start}}, \rv{w}^1, \ldots, \rv{w}^{\ell-1})} + \eqcolor{0} \tag{by \Cref{obs:inter-H2fake-list}-\ref{item:wend-indep-H2fake}} \\
	&\hspace{30pt}\leqslant 6(n_{r-1})^2 \cdot  \sqrt{\frac{s}{2(\beta_r + 1)}}. \qedhere \tag{by \Cref{clm:inter-H2fake}}
\end{align*}

\label{fact:it-facts}
  Let $\rv{A}$, $\rv{B}$, $\rv{C}$, and $\rv{D}$ be four (possibly correlated) random variables.
   \begin{enumerate}
  \item \label{part:uniform} $0 \leqslant \en{\rv{A}} \leqslant \log{\card{\supp{\rv{A}}}}$. The right equality holds
    iff $\distribution{\rv{A}}$ is uniform.
  \item \label{part:info-zero} $\mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}} \geqslant 0$. The equality holds iff $\rv{A}$ and
    $\rv{B}$ are \emph{independent} conditioned on $\rv{C}$.
    \item \label{part:info-entropy} $\mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}} \leqslant \en{\rv{B}}$ for any random variables $\rv{A}, \rv{B}, \rv{C}$. 
  \item \label{part:cond-reduce} \emph{Conditioning on a random variable reduces entropy}:
    $\en{\rv{A} \mid \rv{B},\rv{C}} \leqslant \en{\rv{A} \mid  \rv{B}}$.  The equality holds iff $\rv{A} \perp \rv{C} \mid \rv{B}$.



  \item \label{part:chain-rule} \emph{Chain rule for mutual information}: $\mi{\rv{A},\rv{B}}{\rv{C} \mid \rv{D}} = \mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{C} \mid \rv{D}} + \mi{\rv{B}}{\rv{C} \mid  \rv{A},\rv{D}}$.
  \item \label{part:data-processing} \emph{Data processing inequality}: for a function $f(\rv{A})$ of $\rv{A}$, $\mi{f(\rv{A})}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}} \leqslant \mi{\rv{A}}{\rv{B} \mid \rv{C}}$. 
   \end{enumerate}

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{fact:tvd-chain-rule}
	For any distributions $\mu$ and $\nu$ on $n$-tuples $(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$, 
	\[
		\tvd{\mu}{\nu} \leqslant \sum_{i=1}^{n} \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{X_{<i} \sim \mu} \tvd{\mu(X_i \mid X_{<i})}{\nu(X_i \mid X_{<i})}. 
	\]

nodes.raw_latex:
First, we prove the equality between the second term and the third term in the statement. 
\begin{align*}
	\tvd{\rv{X}\rv{Z}}{\rv{Y}\rv{Z}} &=\frac12 \cdot \sum_{W, Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[(W, Z)] \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X}\rv{Z} = (W, Z)] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y}\rv{Z}=(W, Z)]}  \\
	&=\frac12 \cdot \sum_{W, Z}  \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Z} = Z] \cdot (\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid  \rv{Z} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \rv{Z}= Z])} \\
	&= \sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Z} =Z] \cdot \frac12 \sum_{W}  \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid  \rv{Z} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \rv{Z}= Z]} \\
	&= \sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Z} =Z] \cdot\tvd{(\rv{X} \mid \rv{Z}= Z)}{(\rv{Y} \mid \rv{Z} = Z)} \\
	&= \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{Z} \tvd{(\rv{X} \mid \rv{Z}= Z)}{(\rv{Y} \mid \rv{Z} = Z)}.
\end{align*}

Now we prove the inequality between the first term and the third term. 
\begin{align*}
		\tvd{\rv{X}}{\rv{Y}} &= \frac12 \cdot \sum_{W} \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W]} \\
		&= \frac12 \cdot \sum_{W} \card{\sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Z} = Z](\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid \rv{Z} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \rv{Z} = Z])} \\
		& \leqslant  \frac12 \cdot \sum_{W}  \sum_{Z} \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Z} = Z] \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid \rv{Z} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \rv{Z} = Z]} \\
		&= \sum_{Z}   \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Z} = Z] \cdot \paren{\frac12 \cdot \sum_{W} \card{\ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{X} = W \mid \rv{Z} = Z] - \ensuremath{\textnormal{Pr}}[\rv{Y} = W \mid \rv{Z} = Z]}}  \\
		&= \ensuremath{{\mathbb{E}}}_{Z} \tvd{\rv{X} \mid \rv{Z}= Z}{\rv{Y} \mid \rv{Z} = Z}. \qedhere
\end{align*}
